pages.text: A clay hearth or lit campfire gives radiant heat. A closed room retains heat after the source goes out. More insulation means slower loss, not an extra heat source.

pages.title: First minutes
pages.text: Start with shelter and existing heat sources. Campfires, hearths and stoves give local radiant heat with line of sight. When fuel is unavailable, an enclosed snow shelter retains body heat.
Use coal or charcoal in fuel-burning fixtures. A chimney improves ventilation; a closed damper reduces it. Doors, gaps and wind change room behavior. Do not expect instant comfort.
